title: Skybase is the Agent that operates Sky.money as a non-custodial AI-powered gateway to the Sky Protocol
content:
A.6.1.1.4.1 defines Skybase as "an Agent specializing in creating accessible and user-friendly DeFi interfaces." Its concrete remit is the Sky.money user interface — "a non-custodial web application serving as a gateway to the Sky Protocol" — plus selected Sky websites on Sky.money subdomains, including the Sky Governance Voting Portal at vote.sky.money.

Two constraints are welded together in the definition. The first is a *mission*: through an AI-powered interface, make digital asset interactions "intuitive and accessible for users of all experience levels." The second is a *prohibition*: "Sky.money never takes custody of users' private keys or assets; users retain full responsibility for managing their private keys and digital wallet access."

The pairing is what makes this load-bearing rather than descriptive. The cheapest way to make DeFi feel simple is to take custody and hide the keys — which is exactly what a custodial exchange does. By writing non-custody into the Agent's founding description rather than leaving it as an implementation choice, the Atlas removes that shortcut from Skybase's design space permanently. Accessibility must be achieved through interface quality, not through absorbing user responsibility.

The voting-portal assignment has a second-order consequence: the same Agent that owns the retail funnel also owns the surface through which SKY holders govern. Interface decisions at Skybase are therefore governance-relevant, not merely commercial.
description: Its accessibility mandate is fenced by a custody rule: Sky.money never holds keys or assets, so ease of onboarding cannot be bought with custodial convenience.
